candidate.answerReason: The unshaded region consists of four unit corner squares and four triangles. Pairing triangles on opposite sides gives total unshaded area 19, leaving shaded area 25−19=6.

methods.label: Subtract the unshaded pieces
methods.explanation:
The unshaded pieces have convenient bases along the grid's boundary, so subtract their areas from the whole square. Let \(P\) be the point where the four blades meet.

[Figure 1](figures/2007_AMC_8_Q23_question_fig1.svg)

The white region consists of four \(1\times1\) corner squares and four triangles, one along each side of the grid. These pieces have disjoint interiors and cover all the unshaded area.

The top and bottom white triangles each have base \(3\), since a unit corner square occupies each end of the corresponding side. Their perpendicular heights, measured from \(P\), add to \(5\), the distance between the top and bottom sides. Their combined area is therefore
\[
\frac12\cdot3\cdot5=\frac{15}{2}.
\]
The left and right triangles likewise have bases \(3\) and heights adding to \(5\), so their combined area is also \(\frac{15}{2}\). This pairing avoids needing the exact location of \(P\).

The whole grid has area \(25\), and the four corner squares have total area \(4\). Hence the shaded area is
\[
25-4-\frac{15}{2}-\frac{15}{2}=\boxed{6}
\]
square units, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses only square area, triangle area, and distances counted on a unit grid. It does not assume that the junction is the grid's center.

candidate.annotationRationale: Finding a shaded composite area by subtracting a complete decomposition of its complement directly assesses cnm_p150. Square and triangle area formulas are supporting knowledge. No congruence or symmetry claim about the blades is needed.

review.mathematicalCheck: The actual figure's complement consists of four unit corner squares and four triangles with boundary bases 3 and common apex P. Opposite triangle heights sum to 5, so the unshaded area is \(4+15/2+15/2=19\). The shaded area is therefore \(25-19=6\).
review.levelCheck: The decomposition and paired-height argument use elementary area reasoning and explain why P's exact location is unnecessary.
